evals.prompt: Coordinate Phase 1 after GF-010 has landed: GF-011, GF-012, and GF-013 are initially ready; GF-012 then becomes terminally blocked.
evals.expected_output: A ledger-backed plan that initially admits all three within capacity, then continues GF-011 and GF-013 while localizing the GF-012 block; GF-014 follows GF-013 and GF-015 waits for GF-011 and GF-014.
assertions: States that GF-012 does not block GF-011 or GF-013 to GF-014, and that GF-015 waits for GF-011 and GF-014
Requires registered worktrees and continuous pairs

evals.prompt: A reviewed story is rebased onto the integration branch after another story lands. What must happen before integration?
evals.expected_output: The same pair creates a new committed candidate, runs affected checks, records ledger evidence, and performs incremental read-only re-review.
assertions: Rejects transfer of the old verdict
Does not require a sealer or clone

evals.prompt: Recover a ledger-listed story worktree in three cases: its exact recorded branch/object exists and reconciles cleanly; the object is missing; or the surviving workspace is dirty/mismatched. Explain whether a fresh clone or hosted-CI checkout can be used.
evals.expected_output: Reattach the clean existing branch/object as a registered worktree; stop OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED for missing or dirty/mismatched facts; reject a local clone and treat hosted CI only as independent CI infrastructure.
assertions: Starts with git worktree list porcelain reconciliation
Reattaches only an exact recorded branch and object at the registered path
Stops on missing objects or dirty and mismatched evidence
Rejects fresh-clone recovery and permits provider-managed checkout only for hosted CI
